parameters.content:
## REGISTRY SYNC — QUICK GUIDE

**1. Purpose**
Registry Sync takes newly discovered companies/career-source candidates — typed in by hand, read from a Google Sheet, or read from an Apify dataset — and safely checks them against our official company registry.
It does NOT collect job postings, and it does NOT figure out which applicant-tracking system (ATS) a company uses. Those happen in other workflows.

**2. Start / configuration**
- Start Registry Sync Run → the manual button you click to run this workflow. It never runs on its own.
- Workflow Configuration → where you set the mode (manual / google_sheets / apify) and other settings before running. For Google Sheets mode, this is also where you set googleSheetSpreadsheetId (which spreadsheet) and googleSheetTabName (which tab) — you never need to edit the Read Google Sheet Candidates node itself to point at a different sheet.
- The Google account Registry Sync reads the sheet as is attached to the Read Google Sheet Candidates node itself, as an n8n Credential — never typed into Workflow Configuration, never stored in this file.
- Generate Discovery Run ID → creates one unique ID for this run, so every candidate checked in this run can be traced back to it later.
- Manual Candidates Input → where you type company details directly. Only used when mode = manual.

**3. Manual scenario (mode = manual)**
Start Registry Sync Run → Workflow Configuration → Generate Discovery Run ID → Manual Candidates Input → Is Manual Mode? → Load Manual Candidates → shared processing (section 6)
- Is Manual Mode? → checks whether mode is set to "manual".
- Load Manual Candidates → reads the companies you typed in and gets them ready to be checked.

**4. Google Sheets scenario (mode = google_sheets)**
Is Manual Mode? (No) → Is Google Sheets Mode? (Yes) → Read Google Sheet Candidates → Extract Google Sheet Candidates → shared processing (section 6)
- Read Google Sheet Candidates → reads every row directly from the configured Google Sheet tab, right at run time. No copying, no pasting, no CSV file needed — you just keep the sheet up to date and run Registry Sync.
- Extract Google Sheet Candidates → gets each row ready to be checked, the same way every other input does.
- The sheet needs a header row with these column names: company_name (required — a row without this is rejected before it reaches the database), and country_code, official_website_url, official_careers_url, company_id_hint, ats_provider_hint (all optional).

**5. Apify scenario (mode = apify)**
Is Manual Mode? (No) → Is Google Sheets Mode? (No) → Fetch Apify Dataset → Evaluate Apify Fetch → retry/wait if needed → Extract Apify Candidates → shared processing (section 6)
- Fetch Apify Dataset → reads a list of companies that Apify already collected earlier. IMPORTANT: this only READS a finished dataset — it does NOT start a new Apify run. The dataset ID is set on purpose by a person before running — never automatic, never guessed.
- Evaluate Apify Fetch → checks whether that read worked.
- Should Retry Apify Fetch? / Compute Apify Backoff / Apify Backoff Wait → if the read failed for a temporary reason (like a timeout), these wait a short time and try again, up to a few times, so one hiccup does not stop the whole run.
- Extract Apify Candidates → pulls the company list out of a successful response.

**6. Shared processing (used by all three scenarios)**
- Normalize Candidates → makes manual, Google Sheets, and Apify data look the same shape, so the rest of the workflow does not need to care where a candidate came from.
- Process Candidates → goes through the candidates one at a time.
- Validate Candidate → checks that the candidate at least has a company name. Nothing else is checked here.
- Is Candidate Valid? → sends valid candidates onward, and sends candidates missing a name to be recorded as failed.
- Resolve Registry Candidate → asks the database to decide: is this a brand-new company/source, an existing one, or unclear? This is the ONLY step that writes to the registry.
- Classify RPC Outcome → reads the database's answer and labels what happened to this candidate.
- Build Validation Failed Result → records a candidate that was missing a name, before it ever reached the database.
- Build Run Summary → once every candidate has been checked, this builds one summary of the whole run.

**7. Possible outcomes**
- created_new → a brand-new company/source was added to the registry.
- resolved_existing → the company/source was already known and was reused — no duplicate was created.
- staged → the candidate is uncertain or incomplete (for example, missing or unrecognized country, or no usable website/careers link), so it was set aside for a person to review instead of guessing and polluting the registry.
- validation_failed → the candidate's own info was invalid (usually a missing name) before it ever reached the database.
- infrastructure_failed → a technical problem (network, timeout, database) happened while checking this candidate. It is safe to run again later.

**8. Important boundaries**
- Registry Sync only discovers/resolves company sources.
- Source Intelligence later classifies unknown sources.
- Job Ingestion later fetches the actual jobs.
- New or uncertain candidates should never bypass Resolve Registry Candidate.
- Discovering a company/source never approves it. Registry Sync cannot set review or approval status — that is always a separate, deliberate action by a person.
- It is safe to run this workflow more than once, or to have two runs overlap — the database (not this workflow) prevents duplicates.
- The database decides if two entries are really the same company/source (using the company, its country, and the source together) — this workflow never guesses that itself.
- A missing or unrecognized country is never blocked by this workflow — that candidate is simply sent to the database, which safely sets it aside for review. Country checking is never duplicated here.
- This workflow should stay switched OFF unless someone is intentionally running or configuring it.
